# crimlab

[![check](https://github.com/rootcoder007/crimlab/actions/workflows/check.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rootcoder007/crimlab/actions/workflows/check.yml)
[![coverage](https://github.com/rootcoder007/crimlab/actions/workflows/coverage.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rootcoder007/crimlab/actions/workflows/coverage.yml)
[![srr](https://github.com/rootcoder007/crimlab/actions/workflows/srr.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rootcoder007/crimlab/actions/workflows/srr.yml)
[![pkgdown](https://github.com/rootcoder007/crimlab/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rootcoder007/crimlab/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yml)

Statistical methods for courts, corrections, policing, forensics and
sociolegal research. The computations run in a compiled C++17 core with
a plain C interface (`src/crimlab.h`); the R functions check their
arguments and call it. Where an identity or a bound has a
machine-checked proof in Lean,
[`proof()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/proof.md)
names the theorem.

![crimlab in one minute: a veil-of-darkness table, a reported odds ratio
checked against every labelling of its table, a clearance paradox, a
categorical audit, a posterior from a likelihood ratio, hot spots,
spatial autocorrelation, the command-line program, and the theorems
behind a function](reference/figures/demo.svg)

crimlab in one minute: a veil-of-darkness table, a reported odds ratio
checked against every labelling of its table, a clearance paradox, a
categorical audit, a posterior from a likelihood ratio, hot spots,
spatial autocorrelation, the command-line program, and the theorems
behind a function

It is written for researchers and analysts in criminology, sociolegal
studies, policing, corrections and forensic science who need these
quantities computed correctly and want to know what each one does and
does not show.
[`vignette("crimlab")`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/articles/crimlab.md)
walks through one example from each family.

## What it takes

The functions work on summary data, not on raw records:

- counts by group: stops, searches, uses of force, offences recorded and
  cleared, residents, offenders and victims;
- individual outcomes coded 0 or 1, with a group or a decision for each
  person: release, sentence, reconviction;
- allele frequencies and genotypes at one or more loci;
- likelihood ratios from validation comparisons whose source is known;
- networks as edge lists of labels (who offended with whom, who passed
  what to whom), or incident tables that list the offenders of each
  incident.
- point locations of incidents, planar or longitude and latitude
  (vectors, tables or sf points), with times, weights or counts by area;
- risk scores with outcomes and groups, trace-evidence measurements,
  event time windows, reported figures, matched-pair differences and
  counts over time.

## What it asks

- Disparities: does visibility change who is stopped, what an odds ratio
  says about risk, whether hit rates can show bias, how a disparity per
  resident splits into contact and force.
- Forensics: how rare a DNA profile is, what a likelihood ratio is worth
  and what it is not, how well a system’s ratios are calibrated,
  kinship, paternity, mixtures and database searches.
- Policing: why an aggregate clearance rate can fall while every offence
  type clears better, what a proxy for exposure allows, what misrecorded
  group membership does, regression to the mean at hot spots.
- Corrections: what incapacitation prevents, what a release rule’s
  failure rate can be when only the released are seen, mean time in
  custody from current stays, and what observational data alone say
  about a sentence’s effect.
- Networks: who co-offends with whom, who sits between groups, which
  offenders form the core and the communities of a network, and how
  cleanly it splits in two.
- Places: where incidents centre and how far they spread, whether they
  cluster more than chance, where the hot spots are, whether places
  close together have similar rates (Geary’s C, the Getis-Ord G, local
  Moran), whether incidents close in space are close in time, and where
  to search first for the base of a series.
- Methods from the forensic and sociolegal literature: the fairness of a
  risk tool by group, the weight of glass and other trace evidence, when
  an event known only within a window happened, whether reported figures
  follow Benford’s law, how strong hidden bias must be to explain a
  matched result away, and group-based trajectories of offending.
- Counts and rates: rate ratios between groups from Poisson and negative
  binomial regression with an exposure, adjustment and cluster-robust or
  GEE standard errors
  ([`cntreg()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/cntreg.md));
  rates and proportions by group with their ratios and differences,
  exact and approximate intervals and over-representation
  ([`grprr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/grprr.md));
  directly standardised rates
  ([`dastd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dastd.md));
  observed over expected counts with funnel limits and empirical Bayes
  shrinkage
  ([`sirex()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/sirex.md)).
- Tables: cross-tabulation of records or of an aggregate table’s counts,
  with chi-square and likelihood-ratio tests, Fisher’s exact test,
  Cramer’s V with its interval, and the share on the diagonal
  ([`ctabx()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ctabx.md)).
- Presets: how the columns of a published dataset (Ontario segregation
  and deaths-in-custody tables, use-of-force files, Special
  Investigations Unit cases, Structured Intervention Unit tables,
  Toronto incident layers) feed these functions, so that
  `cntreg(clprep(data, "otis-c01-cnt"))` gives the published analysis
  ([`clprep()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/clprep.md)).
  The risk-tool audits
  ([`fairdf()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/fairdf.md),
  [`tmpaud()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/tmpaud.md),
  [`calaud()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/calaud.md),
  [`scrdsp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/scrdsp.md))
  take presets the same way. Presets describe layouts and ship no data.
- Audits of risk tools and predictive policing: how a tool’s decisions
  differ between groups, with intervals
  ([`fairdf()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/fairdf.md)),
  over time and place
  ([`tmpaud()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/tmpaud.md));
  whether an algorithm ranks areas in the order of what was then
  recorded there, and whether the disagreement follows the areas’ groups
  ([`calaud()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/calaud.md),
  [`scrdsp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/scrdsp.md));
  whether similar people get similar scores
  ([`lipaud()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/lipaud.md));
  what a noisily recorded base rate says about the true one
  ([`nsbnd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/nsbnd.md));
  the false positive rate the other rates force
  ([`impfpr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/impfpr.md));
  which pairs a noisy ranking orders
  ([`rnkres()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/rnkres.md));
  the Oaxaca-Blinder split of a gap
  ([`oaxbd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/oaxbd.md));
  and simulated records with a known disparity to try them on
  ([`fairsim()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/fairsim.md),
  [`nordet()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/nordet.md)).
  They describe what a tool or an agency did, not why.
- Checks: which labelling of a table reproduces a reported odds ratio,
  risk ratio or risk difference
  ([`relchk()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/relchk.md)),
  and what the functions here would make of categorical inputs before an
  analysis
  ([`catchk()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/catchk.md)).

## Algorithms

Every method is a published one, cited on its help page; none is new,
and the package does not claim to be the first implementation of any of
them in R. What it adds is a single checked implementation: arguments
are checked in R and again in the compiled kernels, quantities that
overflow or cancel in the obvious formula are computed in a stable form,
and most functions rest on identities or bounds proved in Lean, which
[`proof()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/proof.md)
names.

## Speed

`dev/bench.R` times each function against every other package found that
computes the same quantity, on fixed seeded inputs and at sizes met in
practice, after checking that the two give the same values;
`dev/bench-net.R` does the same for the network functions. The search
for those packages, with the reason each candidate does or does not
compute the same quantity, is
[inst/bench/counterparts.csv](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/inst/bench/counterparts.csv)
(written by `dev/cpart.R`). rmorie, the maintainer’s own package, is
timed too but reported apart: it is not another package. Where no
package computes a quantity, the function is timed against rmorie or a
base-R implementation of the formula, and no claim is made against the
field. The tables, with the machine, its load during each run and the
spread over three runs, are
[inst/bench/bench.md](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/inst/bench/bench.md)
(and `bench.csv`) and `inst/bench/net.csv`. The lists below are written
by the same scripts from those tables. The spatial functions and the
learners have speed tables of their own, `inst/bench/sp.csv`
(`dev/bench-sp.R`) and `inst/bench/dml.csv`; the three name their
columns alike.

Faster, by at least a tenth, than every other package found that
computes the same quantity, at every size timed:
[`gtmp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/gtmp.md),
[`mixlr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/mixlr.md),
[`cllr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/cllr.md),
[`cllrmin()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/cllrmin.md),
[`eceplt()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/eceplt.md),
[`clrsmp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/clrsmp.md).

Not faster than another package at some size timed:
[`kinidx()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/kinidx.md),
[`patidx()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/patidx.md),
[`lrcal()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/lrcal.md).

No other package found that computes the same quantity, so no claim of
speed against the field:
[`vodtst()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/vodtst.md),
[`orrisk()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/orrisk.md),
[`outtst()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/outtst.md),
[`dspbm()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dspbm.md),
[`dyadrt()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dyadrt.md),
[`expbnd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/expbnd.md),
[`misrd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/misrd.md),
[`rtmhs()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/rtmhs.md),
[`incap()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/incap.md),
[`incapr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/incapr.md),
[`sellab()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/sellab.md),
[`losbnd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/losbnd.md),
[`sntbnd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/sntbnd.md),
[`hzdsel()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/hzdsel.md),
[`lrpost()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/lrpost.md),
[`dbsrch()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dbsrch.md),
[`tipplt()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/tipplt.md),
[`proof()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/proof.md).
Of these, compared with rmorie, the maintainer’s own package: faster at
every size timed:
[`vodtst()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/vodtst.md),
[`orrisk()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/orrisk.md),
[`outtst()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/outtst.md),
[`dspbm()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dspbm.md),
[`dyadrt()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dyadrt.md),
[`expbnd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/expbnd.md),
[`misrd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/misrd.md),
[`rtmhs()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/rtmhs.md),
[`incapr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/incapr.md),
[`sellab()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/sellab.md),
[`losbnd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/losbnd.md),
[`sntbnd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/sntbnd.md),
[`hzdsel()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/hzdsel.md);
not faster at some size:
[`incap()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/incap.md).
Compared with a base-R implementation of the formula: faster at every
size timed:
[`dbsrch()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dbsrch.md),
[`proof()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/proof.md);
not faster at some size:
[`lrpost()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/lrpost.md),
[`tipplt()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/tipplt.md).

Networks, against igraph, sna, tnet and netmem: faster, by at least a
tenth, than every package that computes the same measure, at every size
timed, counting only the measure on a graph the other package has
already built:
[`ntcls()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntcls.md),
[`ntevc()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntevc.md),
[`ntcmp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntcmp.md),
[`ntlvn()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntlvn.md),
[`ntmod()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntmod.md),
[`ntbrk()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntbrk.md),
[`coofg()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/coofg.md).
Not faster at some size by that count:
[`ntdeg()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntdeg.md),
[`ntbtw()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntbtw.md),
[`ntcore()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntcore.md);
of these, counting the building of the other package’s graph from the
same labels, which crimlab’s time includes, faster at every size:
[`ntcore()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntcore.md).
No other package found:
[`ntchg()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntchg.md).

## Life cycle

Experimental. This is a development version: function names, arguments
and results may change before a first release.

## Installation

From GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("rootcoder007/crimlab")
```

The package needs a C++17 compiler and no R package beyond those that
ship with R.

## Examples

### Disparities in policing

``` r

library(crimlab)

# veil of darkness: does visibility change who is stopped?
vodtst(day = c(white = 600, black = 400), night = c(white = 700, black = 300))

# the same counts from a data frame: groups are matched by name, never by
# position, and a table with day and night columns can be given whole
stops <- data.frame(race = c("white", "black", "white", "black"),
                    light = c("day", "day", "night", "night"),
                    n = c(600, 400, 700, 300))
vodtst(xtabs(n ~ race + light, stops), ref = "white")

# the risks, and the relative risk, behind an odds ratio
orrisk(or = 3, rate = 0.4, share = 0.5)

# outcome test: stop and hit rates at a search threshold
outtst(q = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9), t = 0.3)

# force per resident = contact per resident x force per contact
dspbm(pop = c(a = 9000, b = 1000), contact = c(a = 900, b = 300),
      force = c(a = 9, b = 6))

# offending rates per offender and per offender-victim pair
pop <- c(a = 800, b = 200)
dyadrt(count = outer(pop, pop) / 1000, pop = pop)
```

### Clearance rates

``` r

# both offence types clear better in B, yet B's aggregate rate is lower
clrsmp(clra = c(minor = 90, serious = 20), reca = c(minor = 100, serious = 50),
       clrb = c(minor = 19, serious = 60), recb = c(minor = 20, serious = 140))
```

### Corrections

``` r

# custody against a community sentence, with no assumption about who got which
y <- c(1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0)
z <- c("community", "community", "custody", "custody", "custody",
       "community", "custody", "community")
sntbnd(y, z, treat = "custody")

# a release rule scored from the outcomes of those the judge released
sellab(y = c(0, 1, 0, NA, NA), rel = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE),
       rule = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
```

### DNA match statistics

``` r

# match probability with the Balding-Nichols correction
gtmp(p = c(D3 = 0.1, vWA = 0.2), q = c(0.3, NA), hom = c(FALSE, TRUE),
     theta = 0.03)

# a likelihood ratio needs a prior before it is a probability
lrpost(lr = 1e6, prior = 1 / 5e6)

# a match found by searching a database
dbsrch(mp = 1e-9, n = 5e6, pop = 3e7)
```

### Kinship, paternity and mixtures

``` r

kinidx(g1 = c(12, 14), g2 = c(12, 14), freq = c(0.1, 0.2), rel = "sibling")
patidx(child = c(12, 14), father = c(14, 15), freq = c(0.1, 0.2),
       mother = c(12, 12))

p <- c(a = 0.1, b = 0.2, c = 0.05, d = 0.15)
mixlr(p, np = character(0), xp = 0, nd = c("c", "d"), xd = 1)
```

### Performance of likelihood ratios

``` r

same <- c(50, 200, 8, 0.5)
diff <- c(0.01, 0.2, 1.5, 0.001)
cllr(same, diff)
cllrmin(same, diff)
lrcal(same, diff)
tipplt(same, diff)
eceplt(same, diff)
```

### Co-offending networks

``` r

# offenders recorded together in an incident are tied, weighted by the
# number of incidents they share
inc <- c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5)
off <- c("ana", "ben", "cy", "ana", "ben", "cy", "dee", "dee", "eli", "fay")
g <- coofg(inc, off)
e <- g$edges
ntdeg(e$from, e$to, w = e$w, nodes = g$nodes)
ntbtw(e$from, e$to, nodes = g$nodes)
ntlvn(e$from, e$to, w = e$w, nodes = g$nodes)
ntbrk(e$from, e$to, grp = c(ana = "x", ben = "x", cy = "x", dee = "y",
                            eli = "y", fay = "z"), nodes = g$nodes)
```

### Spatial input

``` r

# planar coordinates (metres, say): two vectors, a matrix or a data frame
# with columns x and y; longitude and latitude only with lonlat = TRUE
set.seed(1)
p <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100, 500, 50), y = rnorm(100, 800, 30))
cgstat(p)
sdell(p, c = 2)

ll <- data.frame(lon = c(-79.40, -79.38, -79.35), lat = c(43.64, 43.66, 43.65))
webpt(ll, lonlat = TRUE)          # the centre comes back in degrees
hvdist(ll, c(-79.38, 43.65))      # great-circle metres
eqproj(ll)                        # equal-area metres for the planar functions

# sf points go in directly; their CRS must agree with lonlat
s <- sf::st_as_sf(ll, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
cgstat(s, lonlat = TRUE)
# and plain results go back to sf
sf::st_as_sf(eqproj(ll), coords = c("x", "y"))
```

The planar functions assume Cartesian coordinates in one length unit and
return lengths in that unit; functions with a `lonlat` argument project
longitude and latitude to metres themselves (an equal-area projection
about the points’ centre) and return centres in degrees; functions that
take a study rectangle (`win`) take planar coordinates only. All are
two-dimensional.

### Hot spots, space-time and journey to crime

``` r

set.seed(2)
x <- c(rnorm(40, 0, 0.3), rnorm(40, 6, 0.3), runif(40, -5, 10))
y <- c(rnorm(40, 0, 0.3), rnorm(40, 6, 0.3), runif(40, -5, 10))
fzmode(x, y, r = 0.5)                               # points within 0.5 of each
nnhclu(x, y, area = 225, p = 0.05, minpts = 5)$clusters
kmpart(x, y, k = 3, seed = 1)$cen
stacel(x, y, win = c(-5, 10, -5, 10), r = 0.75, top = 10, minpts = 5)$clusters
mantst(x, y, t = seq_along(x), nsim = 199, seed = 1)
mantst(x, y, t = seq_along(x), nsim = 199, seed = 1, metric = "manhattan")
hdbang(x, y, v = fzmode(x, y, r = 0.5))      # head-bang smoothing
crwalk(cbind(x = x[1:10], y = y[1:10]), h = 2, seed = 1)$msd
# clusters relative to a population at risk; zones as counts at centroids
rnnhcl(x, y, base = cbind(x = runif(500, -5, 10), y = runif(500, -5, 10)),
       h = 1, minpts = 5)$clusters
fzmode(x[1:20], y[1:20], r = 1, count = rpois(20, 3))

# a search priority over a grid, not evidence about any person
s <- jtsurf(c(2, 3, 4), c(2, 4, 3), win = c(0, 6, 0, 6), nx = 30, ny = 30,
            type = "negexp", par = c(1, 1), mode = "lik")
jtacc(s$prob, win = c(0, 6, 0, 6), base = c(3.2, 2.9))
```

### Spatial weights and autocorrelation

``` r

set.seed(4)
p <- cbind(x = runif(60), y = runif(60))
v <- ifelse(p[, 1] > 0.7 & p[, 2] > 0.7, 5, 1) + rnorm(60, sd = 0.3)
w <- spwt(p, k = 5)                    # or type = "band", or "contig"
gearc(v, w)                            # Geary's C
gorg(v, spwt(p, type = "band", d = 0.2, style = "raw"))   # global G
head(lmorn(v, w, nsim = 199, seed = 1))                    # local Moran
locgi(v, spwt(p, type = "band", d = 0.2, style = "raw"))  # local G*
dirmn(p, origin = c(0.5, 0.5))         # directional mean from an origin
```

### Risk tools, trace evidence, time and data screens

``` r
set.seed(3)
g <- rep(c("a", "b"), each = 100)
y <- rbinom(200, 1, ifelse(g == "a", 0.3, 0.5))
s <- plogis(rnorm(200, ifelse(y == 1, 0.8, -0.8)))
fair(s, y, g)$met                     # error rates and predictive values by group

rswp(rnorm(50, 0.5), gam = c(1, 1.5, 2))   # how much hidden bias explains it away
bnft(bdig(exp(runif(500, 0, 10)))$dig)$stat
gstr(matrix(rpois(100, 2), 10))[1:3, ]
sptst(rpois(30, 10), rpois(30, 10), nboot = 199, seed = 1)$glob
### Audits of risk tools and predictive policing

```r
d <- fairsim(4000, nareas = 24, bias = 0.5, seed = 1)  # a known disparity
fairdf(d$det, d$group, base = "A")$tab[, c("group", "dp", "di", "dilo", "dihi")]
calaud(d$area, d$risk, d$det, d$group, nperm = 499, seed = 1)$groups
scrdsp(d$risk, d$group)$anova
nsbnd(c(a = 0.35, b = 0.55), a = 0.1, b = 0.2)$pairs   # ordered under noise?
impfpr(p = c(a = 0.3, b = 0.5), ppv = 0.6, fnr = 0.25)  # Chouldechova
oaxbd(d$risk, d$truth, d$group, ref = "A")$dec
```

### Checking reports and inputs

``` r

# which reference group and event give a reported odds ratio of 0.44?
tab <- matrix(c(20, 10, 80, 90), 2,
              dimnames = list(c("A", "B"), c("yes", "no")))
relchk(tab, 0.44, ref = "B", event = "yes")

# missing values, unused and rare levels, labels that differ by case, and
# the reference level a default would take
d <- data.frame(sex = c("Male", "male", "Female", "Female", NA),
                custody = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
catchk(d, nmin = 2)
```

### Proofs

``` r

proof("vodtst")
```

## Checking the proofs

The Lean 4 files are in `inst/lean` (installed under
`system.file("lean", package = "crimlab")`). With
[elan](https://github.com/leanprover/elan) installed:

``` sh
cd inst/lean
lake exe cache get   # prebuilt Mathlib, about 5 GB
lake build
```

A build with no error and no `sorry` is the check.

## Citation

`citation("crimlab")` gives the reference for the installed version:

> Ruhela, V. S. (2026). *crimlab: Criminology and Sociolegal
> Statistics.* R package. <https://github.com/rootcoder007/crimlab>

## Licence

Apache License 2.0 with LLVM Exceptions; see `LICENSE`. The SPDX
identifier is `Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception`. The exception lets
compiled code that embeds the kernels be redistributed without the
attribution conditions, and settles linking with GPL-2 software.

## Python

`py/` holds a Python package, also named crimlab, that compiles the same
kernels from `src/` and gives the same functions, argument names and
results; its tests check every number against the R package. It has no
runtime dependencies. Install it from a clone with `pip install ./py`;
see `py/README.md` for how inputs are matched by name and the few
differences from R.

# Package index

## Disparities

Veil of darkness, odds ratios and risks, the outcome test, benchmarks
and dyadic rates.

- [`vodtst()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/vodtst.md)
  : Veil-of-darkness test
- [`orrisk()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/orrisk.md)
  : Risks behind an odds ratio
- [`outtst()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/outtst.md)
  : Outcome test
- [`dspbm()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dspbm.md)
  : Benchmark decomposition of a disparity
- [`dyadrt()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dyadrt.md)
  : Dyadic offending rates

## Forensics

DNA match statistics, the weight and calibration of likelihood ratios,
kinship, paternity, mixtures and database searches.

- [`gtmp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/gtmp.md) :
  Genotype match probability
- [`lrpost()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/lrpost.md)
  : Posterior probability from a likelihood ratio
- [`cllr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/cllr.md) :
  Log-likelihood-ratio cost
- [`cllrmin()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/cllrmin.md)
  : Log-likelihood-ratio cost after recalibration
- [`lrcal()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/lrcal.md)
  : Calibrated likelihood ratios
- [`tipplt()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/tipplt.md)
  : Tippett plot
- [`eceplt()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/eceplt.md)
  : Empirical cross-entropy plot
- [`mixlr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/mixlr.md)
  : Mixture likelihood ratio
- [`kinidx()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/kinidx.md)
  : Kinship index
- [`patidx()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/patidx.md)
  : Paternity index
- [`dbsrch()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dbsrch.md)
  : Database search

## Policing

Clearance rates, exposure proxies, misrecorded groups and regression to
the mean.

- [`clrsmp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/clrsmp.md)
  : Clearance-rate decomposition and Simpson's paradox
- [`expbnd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/expbnd.md)
  : Rates and disparities when exposure is measured by a proxy
- [`misrd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/misrd.md)
  : Risk difference when group membership is misrecorded
- [`rtmhs()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/rtmhs.md)
  : Regression to the mean at selected hot spots

## Corrections

Incapacitation, release rules, time in custody, sentence effects and
hazards after selection.

- [`incap()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/incap.md)
  : Incapacitation: crime rate, share prevented and the marginal year
- [`incapr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/incapr.md)
  : Incapacitation under desistance and replacement
- [`sellab()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/sellab.md)
  : Evaluating a release rule from the released alone
- [`losbnd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/losbnd.md)
  : Mean time in custody from completed and current stays
- [`sntbnd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/sntbnd.md)
  : Bounds on a sentence's effect without assumptions
- [`hzdsel()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/hzdsel.md)
  : Period-two hazards after selective depletion

## Networks

Co-offending graphs, centrality, cores, components, communities,
brokerage and the Cheeger bounds.

- [`coofg()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/coofg.md)
  : Co-offending graph from an incident table
- [`ntdeg()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntdeg.md)
  : Degree and strength of each node
- [`ntbtw()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntbtw.md)
  : Betweenness of each node
- [`ntcls()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntcls.md)
  : Closeness of each node
- [`ntevc()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntevc.md)
  : Eigenvector centrality of each node
- [`ntcore()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntcore.md)
  : k-core of each node
- [`ntcmp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntcmp.md)
  : Connected components
- [`ntlvn()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntlvn.md)
  : Communities by the Louvain method
- [`ntmod()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntmod.md)
  : Modularity of a partition
- [`ntbrk()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntbrk.md)
  : Brokerage roles
- [`ntchg()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ntchg.md)
  : Cheeger bounds on a network's bottleneck

## Spatial

Distances and projection, centrography, nearest neighbours and K
functions, hot spots, space-time tests and journey to crime.

- [`hvdist()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/hvdist.md)
  : Great-circle distance
- [`eqproj()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/eqproj.md)
  [`eqinv()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/eqproj.md)
  : Equal-area projection of longitude and latitude, and its inverse
- [`cgstat()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/cgstat.md)
  : Mean centre and dispersion of points
- [`cgmedn()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/cgmedn.md)
  : Median centre of points
- [`webpt()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/webpt.md)
  : Centre of minimum distance
- [`sdell()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/sdell.md)
  : Standard deviational ellipse
- [`cvhull()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/cvhull.md)
  : Convex hull of points
- [`nnidx()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/nnidx.md)
  : Nearest-neighbour index
- [`ripk()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ripk.md) :
  Ripley's K function
- [`ripenv()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ripenv.md)
  : Envelopes of Ripley's L function and a test of complete spatial
  randomness
- [`fzmode()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/fzmode.md)
  : Fuzzy mode
- [`kmpart()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/kmpart.md)
  : K-means partition of points
- [`nnhclu()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/nnhclu.md)
  : Nearest-neighbour hierarchical clustering
- [`stacel()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/stacel.md)
  : Search-circle hot-spot areas
- [`rnnhcl()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/rnnhcl.md)
  : Risk-adjusted nearest-neighbour hierarchical clustering
- [`hdbang()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/hdbang.md)
  : Head-bang smoothing
- [`crwalk()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/crwalk.md)
  : Correlated random walk of a series of events
- [`mantst()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/mantst.md)
  : Mantel's space-time test
- [`stmavg()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/stmavg.md)
  : Spatial-temporal moving average
- [`jtdecay()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/jtdecay.md)
  : Distance-decay functions for journey to crime
- [`jtsurf()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/jtsurf.md)
  : Journey-to-crime surface
- [`jtcal()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/jtcal.md)
  : Empirical distance decay from solved trips
- [`jtacc()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/jtacc.md)
  : Accuracy of a journey-to-crime surface on a solved series
- [`bjtc()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/bjtc.md) :
  Bayesian journey to crime
- [`spwt()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/spwt.md) :
  Spatial weights
- [`gearc()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/gearc.md)
  : Geary's C
- [`gorg()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/gorg.md) :
  The general G of Getis and Ord
- [`lmorn()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/lmorn.md)
  : Local Moran (LISA)
- [`locgi()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/locgi.md)
  : Local G and G\* of Getis and Ord
- [`dirmn()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dirmn.md)
  : Directional mean and circular variance

## Dossier methods

Fairness of risk tools, trace evidence, aoristic time, Benford screens,
glass grouping and transfer, constant reporters, sensitivity bounds,
trajectory models, lowess, tool marks, grid Gi\* and the point pattern
test.

- [`fair()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/fair.md) :
  Fairness metrics of a binary risk tool by group
- [`tlvc()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/tlvc.md)
  [`tlvlr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/tlvc.md)
  : Two-level model for multivariate trace evidence
- [`aorwt()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/aorwt.md)
  : Aoristic weights
- [`bdig()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/bdig.md)
  [`bnft()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/bdig.md) :
  Benford digit screens
- [`skp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/skp.md) :
  Scott-Knott grouping of measurements
- [`rptc()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/rptc.md) :
  Constant reporters of a reporting panel
- [`rswp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/rswp.md)
  [`rshl()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/rswp.md) :
  Rosenbaum sensitivity bounds for matched pairs
- [`zgll()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/zgll.md)
  [`zgem()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/zgll.md) :
  Group-based trajectory model for counts
- [`mvtll()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/mvtll.md)
  [`mvtem()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/mvtll.md)
  : Group-based multivariate trajectories
- [`tfrp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/tfrp.md) :
  Glass fragments recovered under transfer and persistence
- [`lwss()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/lwss.md) :
  Lowess smoothing
- [`chmb()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/chmb.md) :
  The Chumbley score for two tool-mark profiles
- [`gstr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/gstr.md) :
  Local Getis-Ord Gi\* on a grid of counts
- [`sptst()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/sptst.md)
  : Andresen's spatial point pattern test

## Risk tools and predictive policing

Differences between groups with intervals, over time and place;
calibration of an area ranking and a score’s spread across groups;
individual fairness; bounds under label noise, Chouldechova’s identity
and the resolution of a ranking; the Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition;
simulated records with a known disparity.

- [`fairdf()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/fairdf.md)
  : Differences between groups in a risk tool's decisions
- [`tmpaud()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/tmpaud.md)
  : Disparity metrics over time and place
- [`calaud()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/calaud.md)
  : Calibration audit of a predictive-policing ranking
- [`scrdsp()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/scrdsp.md)
  : A risk score's spread across groups
- [`lipaud()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/lipaud.md)
  : Individual fairness: a Lipschitz audit
- [`nsbnd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/nsbnd.md)
  : A true base rate behind a noisily recorded one
- [`impfpr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/impfpr.md)
  : The false positive rate the other rates imply
- [`rnkres()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/rnkres.md)
  : Which pairs a noisy ranking orders
- [`oaxbd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/oaxbd.md)
  : Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition of a gap between two groups
- [`fairsim()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/fairsim.md)
  : Simulated records with a known disparity
- [`nordet()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/nordet.md)
  : Noisy-OR detection by patrols

## Checks

Which labelling of a table reproduces a reported contrast, and an audit
of categorical inputs.

- [`relchk()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/relchk.md)
  : Which labelling reproduces a reported contrast?
- [`catchk()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/catchk.md)
  : Audit categorical inputs before an analysis

## Counts, rates and tables

Rate ratios from count regression with exposure and clusters; rates and
proportions by group with exact and approximate intervals; direct and
indirect standardisation; cross-tabulation with tests and measures of
association.

- [`cntreg()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/cntreg.md)
  : Count regression: rate ratios between groups
- [`grprr()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/grprr.md)
  : Rates and proportions by group: ratios and differences
- [`dastd()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dastd.md)
  : Directly standardised rates
- [`sirex()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/sirex.md)
  : Indirect standardisation: standardised ratios with shrinkage
- [`ctabx()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/ctabx.md)
  : Cross-tabulation with tests and measures of association

## Presets

A published dataset’s columns onto a generic function’s arguments.

- [`clprep()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/clprep.md)
  : Presets: a published dataset's columns onto a generic function's
  arguments

## Learning

The elastic net with cross-validation, logistic regression and random
forests; the learners of the cross-fitted estimators.

- [`enpath()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/enpath.md)
  : Elastic net by coordinate descent, with cross-validation
- [`lgtreg()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/lgtreg.md)
  : Logistic regression
- [`rfor()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/rfor.md) :
  Random forest for regression and probabilities

## Causal estimates

Double machine learning by cross-fitting, with the learners above;
augmented inverse probability weighting and targeted maximum likelihood
from the same nuisances.

- [`dmlx()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/dmlx.md) :
  Double machine learning by cross-fitting

## Proofs

- [`proof()`](https://rootcoder007.github.io/crimlab/reference/proof.md)
  : Machine-checked proofs behind the package
